for_senior_author: Risk of bias re-appraised with the editors' narrative-review checklist (instrument none-applicable) in place of AMSTAR 2, which the design does not take. Overall is now high (the worst domain, systematic search and explicit selection), in place of the AMSTAR 2 critically low confidence. This is an instrument correction, not a change of view about the paper: domains are high / some-concerns / low / some-concerns / some-concerns. My five judgments agree with the reader's, so no domain is in dispute.

Three reporting issues keep a cross-paper half that no reader has checked, now marked as such on the card: the Lappin et al. (2017) Table 3 relative risks in reporting issue 2, the claim that the corresponding sentence in Kevil et al. (2019) carries no citation in reporting issue 4, and the stroke-type reading of the 2-to-5-fold estimate in reporting issue 6. They should be closed when sc_lappin_2017 and sc_kevil_2019 are read.

New reporting issue 7 records that the abstract's 'more common type' statement rests on the share of published case reports. Whether interpretation_gap should also carry that inference is a judgment left to the senior author. The same inference is recorded on sc_paulus_2020.
